summary: The core finding holds: AddBiomechanics GRF are measured force-plate data assigned to the feet, not predictions. The range, layout, size and original-source claims also check out. Two things need fixing before the decision reaches José. (1) The 'extra rows' attribution points at the wrong code. The legacy LocoHub files were written by earlier converters that emit one row per frame from processingPasses[1]. The one-raw-row-plus-one-row-per-pass expansion is in the current source-preservation adapter, which produced none of the legacy files. (2) That same expansion applies to option C's outputs, so C's consequence must state the output rows and storage. José's stated reason for avoiding AddBiomechanics was rows and storage, and that cost is currently not shown.

evidence: PLoS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0295152 (publisher HTML, read by me): 'Ground reaction forces are recorded from force plates embedded in the ground'; 'We assign loads from each force plate to the feet in the model based on when the feet are penetrating the ground'; 'Since the ground reaction forces are known from experimental data'; 'the center of pressure locations are fixed based on the ground reaction force data'. No GRF prediction for experimental trials.

ECCV 2024 / arXiv 2406.18537 (HTML): 'Each of these frames contains optical marker locations and ground reaction moment and force measurements'; 'Each raw data source includes experimental optical motion capture and force plate data'. Force estimation appears only as the benchmark ('estimating physical forces from an observed movement', section 5), with no statement that baseline predictions are released.
nimblephysics docs: groundContactForce is 'the ground-reaction force from a contact, measured on the force plate'; missingGRFReason text matches the worker's quote.

SubjectOnDisk.proto at c405b056: I fetched it, and its sha256 is 37c6c94d...54bf, equal to the worker's. Line 187: 'the original force-plate data in world space, one per ground contact body'. Line 228: 'the raw force plate readings, per force plate, without any assignment to feet or any post-processing'. The MissingGRFReason enum (lines 5-17) includes manualReview=10 and footContactDetectedButNoForce=11.

Nuance, not a defect: the ECCV text says frames with steps off force plates are 'discarded' from the analysis, while the B3D keeps such frames flagged. Subject29 shows this: 48 of 64 frames are flagged. So 'kept and flagged' is right at the file level.

checks.area: converter row multiplication (attribution of extra rows)
evidence: The current contributor_tools/conversion_scripts/AddBiomechanics/convert_addbiomechanics_to_parquet.py extract_frame_data (lines ~99-106) emits one raw_frame row (source_pass_index -1) plus one row per processing pass, i.e. 1+P rows per frame. The worker's description of that code is correct.

However, the legacy files were not made by it. The consolidated converter at cc94be4 ('Consolidate AddBiomechanics conversion into unified script'), lines 128-140 and the frame loop near line 310, and the older _archive/b3d_to_parquet.py (line 116) both append one record per frame using frame.processingPasses[1]. They also default mass to 70 kg, which the current adapter explicitly forbids.

So per-pass row expansion cannot explain extra rows in the legacy LocoHub files. Candidates that remain are the retained GRF-flagged frames (48/64 in Subject29) and continuous native-rate frames. The worker's other listed causes (GRF-flagged frames kept; segment cropping) stand, unverified against legacy files.

Related legacy finding for HIST-01/02, not checked further: processingPasses[1] was commented 'Use dynamics processing pass', but in Subject29 the global pass order is [kinematics(0), lowPassFilter(2), dynamics(1)] (my parse). Index 1 is therefore the low-pass pass, not dynamics, for such subjects.
